about: Generated by website/admin/ideas.mjs from website/versions/index.md. Do not edit. next holds the notes of a build that has no number yet: the running build, if its own version is not listed; nextArt its release cards.
next: SGit CRM, first step: the app shell in Apps/CRM, with its own project and workflow (crm-app.yml), bundle ai.sgit.crm.app, for iPhone and iPad. A sidebar of the places the CRM will have (follow-ups, people, organisations, introductions, drafts, import), each saying it is not built yet and which step builds it. No TestFlight until the App Store Connect record exists.

SGit CRM, second step: the record format, sgit.ai/crm/v1. One small JSON file per record in a vault (people, organisations, interactions, introductions, follow-ups, drafts, plays), each value with where it came from, every change saying who made it and an agent always naming its key. Introductions and drafts are records of their own, and only a person can mark a draft sent. The format. Nothing on screen yet.

SGit CRM, third step: import from a vault. The app keeps your CRM in a vault on the device. Import opens another vault by its key or a QR code, finds what looks like contacts (vCards, spreadsheets saved as CSV, JSON lists, CRM records, and photos of business cards and badges, read on the device), and shows each as a proposal, marked when it looks like someone you already have. Accept, change or drop them, one by one or all at once; what you accept is kept in one signed commit, with a note of where you met and a follow-up for each new person if you want them. People and Organisations show what is kept, each detail with where it came from. It also reads the Web Summit team CRM's own layout (contacts, their companies, stages, owners and next steps) and a vault that lists other vaults, such as crm-sources, asking which of them to read; records sealed to the team's keys are listed as not readable yet. Not yet tried on a device.

SGit CRM, how it is put together, at the owner's request: workflows made of cells. A cell is one unit of work (code, a call to Apple's models on the device, a call to Claude behind a lane, an agent, or a person's decision); cells make workflows, workflows make plays, plays make the CRM, and workflows are what we sell. Ten workflows for the Web Summit follow-up, after the ten mapped for Algarve Evolution; the first, import from a vault, is built.

SGit CRM: agreed with the email AgenticCell how the CRM will work with its copy of the mailbox (people joined by email address, a small change file per sync, a reference to the CRM's draft carried through to the send result), and the signed lane entries the CRM will propose replies with, checked against the email cell's own test vector. Nothing sends.

notes: CI for SGit CRM: a push that only changes Apps/CRM no longer starts the VoiceDebrief Mac job (the CRM has its own workflow), and external TestFlight knows the CRM (ai.sgit.crm.app), off until the owner has created its App Store Connect app and set CRM_APP_TESTFLIGHT=1.

SGit CRM started, at the owner's request: a third app in this repository for iPhone and iPad, first used to follow up the contacts and actions from Web Summit, with contacts brought in through import workflows that use vaults. Set up as a cell (cells/crm-ios/: objective, deliverable, behaviour policy, brief) with its own builder session; issue 400. App Store name SGit CRM, bundle id ai.sgit.crm.app. No app code yet.

SGit Secrets, third step: what a secret is (its kinds, its fields, the file it is kept in) and the strong-password maker move out of SGit Vaults into a package both apps can share. Nothing changes in SGit Vaults.

From the owner's memos on 0.1.133. Live: Full details on a memo opens it all at once, your words, the picture that went with it, Claude's answers with their pictures, a small diagram of the sequence of events with each step's time, and the timeline. The picture sent with a note is now kept with it. Agents: sub-tabs by topic, with Waiting for input first, gathering every waiting agent from every project; live counts replace the old drawing; tap an agent for its details and a box to write to it, which goes to Claude to pass on. The right-hand side shows an Update button when a newer build is in TestFlight. Messages to Claude opens large on an iPad, your memos and their answers first and Claude's other messages below, with pictures.

From the owner's memo on 0.1.133: on an iPad or a Mac the timer and the record or finish button stay pinned at the top of the left column while recording, and only the words scroll under them, so the button no longer scrolls away. Tapping the picture attached to a note opens it full screen (pinch or double tap to zoom, Done to close).
SGit Secrets: the vault engine now also reads a merge that the sgit command made itself, checked in the tests with a vault sgit merged after two copies changed apart.

The microphone check now reaches Claude: the transcription step started each note from a fresh record and dropped it (seen on a silent note from 0.1.131). It also shows on each memo's card in the Live panel.

SGit Secrets, second building block: when two devices changed a vault while apart, their changes are now joined. Different secrets merge on their own; a secret changed on both keeps the newer change and the older one beside it, so nothing is lost; a change is never undone by a deletion on the other device. Nothing on screen yet.

SGit Secrets, first building block: a vault can now be written as one file and read back safely (anything that could escape the vault's folders is refused), two copies that changed apart can be joined, and a file is replaced in one step with five earlier copies kept. It is the store the secrets app will keep in iCloud Drive; nothing on screen yet.

The secrets app has a name and decisions: SGit Secrets; pay as you go with credit, a £5 starter switching on a server copy; vaults shared between people only through the server, with keys exchanged between them, never a shared iCloud folder. The plan now starts with the one-file store, and sharing comes with the server in a second version. Read it.

Each recorded note now carries a short microphone check, sent with it: the recorder's loudest reading, the live engine's loudest sample, which microphone it used, and whether the note was rescued from the live audio. A fifth silent note came in on 0.1.126; this says which part went deaf.

Decided (d5): vault keys are kept in iCloud Keychain by default in both apps, with a switch to keep them on one device, as both apps already do; the passkey door comes on top. The sgit app's design page said "this device only" and now says what the app does.
The Live panel also follows memos sent to the owner's own lane to Claude (a contact whose name starts with Claude), not only the built-in developer lane.

Silent recordings: two of the owner's notes tonight (16 s and 63 s, 0.1.123) and earlier ones were pure digital silence, the recorder writing zeros while the live words' audio engine held the microphone. Now the live engine's own audio is kept beside the note while it records, and if the recorder's file turns out silent while the engine heard sound, the note is made from the engine's audio instead, so the words are not lost. While that happens the screen says the recording is being kept from the live audio, and the live words keep running. A flaky test fixed (a server's id could contain the test token).

The right of the record screen on an iPad or a Mac is now tabs, at the owner's request: Live (memos to Claude and their answers), Updates (what Claude sends without being asked, by stream: progress, builds, the newsroom, with pictures), Agents (everyone working for you, grouped by project, with a count of who is working or waiting and what each is doing) and Notes (your recent notes and the rest of the app). Each tab shows a red count of what is new since you last opened it, and the app remembers the tab. The line between the two columns can be dragged to give either side more room, and the split is remembered; a double tap puts it back. All of it comes from the agents vault you gave Claude: nobody else using the app sees it.

Live with Claude, on the right of the record screen on an iPad or a Mac, for the owner's demo: each memo sent to Claude is a card with its status (sending, sent, Claude has it, answered), a clock running from the send until the answer, Claude's answer under it with a picture when one comes, and a timeline you can open showing each step and how long it took (recorded, written up, sent, reached Claude, answered, shown here), drawn as bars on one time line. While the panel is on screen it checks the agents vault every ten seconds and says when it last looked. Clear hides the memos so far.

Inbox: a decision you answered can be changed ("Change"), and the new choice goes to Claude too. External TestFlight: every green build now goes to external testers (the owner's decision in the Inbox), replacing one still waiting for review; [internal] in a commit message keeps one back.

The sgit app opens a vault in its own app when it has one, full screen, with an App and Files switch; shows a vault of photos as a gallery you swipe through, and can add a gallery page to it so it opens as a gallery on the web too; moves several files or folders to another folder in one change; marks each file as on this device or still on the server; opens a photo or video full screen when tapped, with (i) for its details; gives a way up from a folder on an iPad or a Mac; and shows a vault under its own name

notes: The workbench opens full screen, not as a pop-up, and straight into the vault's own app (its chat and pages) rather than its file list, at the owner's request.

A Lab experiment, L07, edit with Apple Intelligence, started small as the owner asked. Give it a text (typed, pasted, or a note's words as a copy) and a request in your own words: make it shorter, more formal, as bullet points, fix the names. Apple's model proposes the edited text, and the app shows the change itself, word by word: what goes is struck through and what comes in is underlined, with the before and the after a tap away. Accept or reject; an accepted change can be put back. It says so when nothing changed or when the result is suspiciously long or short. The note the words came from is never changed. In test: no edit has been asked of a model. Also written up, with no code: what it would take to play YouTube videos in the app, to connect Spotify or Apple Music, and which other accounts are worth connecting (issue 051).

The voice games take their place in the app's one microphone turn: Listen and the voice player hold it while they listen or speak and give it back however they stop, so a voice field, the Lab and a game never listen at once; if something else holds it, the game says so. The game's text field has the shared voice button.

A voice button on text fields, at the owner's request: a small microphone beside a field fills it by speech on this device, the words appearing as they are said after anything already typed; tap again to stop, and the text stays editable. One microphone for the whole app: a field, the Lab's control centre and its live labels take turns, and whichever asks second is told something else is listening or speaking; never while a note is being recorded, and it stops when the app leaves the foreground. On the Lab's prompt and instructions, Your words, a vault's name, a contact's name and the key's name; not on keys, tokens or links.

A new article at the owner's request, three layers: the app's code, Apple's model on the device and agents in a loop, what each is good and bad at (cost, privacy, speed), examples from what exists at each, and how a voice note moves between them, with a drawing. A short version is in the app under Guide, Articles; an article can now carry a short.md for the apps.

notes: Two more Lab experiments, from the owner's memo of the morning. L06, task discovery: ask about your own data (what are my tasks, what happened with the memo I sent yesterday, what is waiting for me) and see it answered in three steps. The question is read for what kind of thing it asks for, by the code's word lists and by Apple's model through one tool for each kind; the code walks a tree of the app's data and shows each branch it entered and each thing it kept or passed over, with the reason; and the answer is put together by the code from what the walk kept. The model is never shown your data and writes none of the answer. L05, talk back: the same, as a conversation by voice. It listens for one question, answers, says the answer aloud, and listens again. Both time every turn and keep a log that can be shared as JSON. In test: no question has been put to a model, and L05 has not been heard on a device.

A voice button on text fields, at the owner's request ("a little voice button everywhere we have an input"): tap the microphone beside a field and speak; the words appear live and stay editable. On the Lab, Your words, vault and contact names, the key name, an agent's message box and the picture sheet's line. Not on the lines added while recording, where the note itself has the microphone.

A voice button on text fields, at the owner's request: a small microphone beside a field fills it by speech on this device, the words appearing as they are said after anything already typed; tap again to stop, and the text stays editable. One listener for every field, never while a note is being recorded, and it stops when the app leaves the foreground. On the Lab's prompt and instructions, Your words, a vault's name, a contact's name and the key's name; not on keys, tokens or links.

From the owner's 11:54 memo: a Pause button beside Finish (the note carries on in the same file; the live words pick up where they stopped); a small counter while recording (time recorded and words heard); "Tune this screen" (the bars' sensitivity and height, the record button's colour, changed live, calmer bars by default); and contacts a conductor offers appear in the Inbox with "Add to Contacts", nothing added until you tap.

On iPhone, a part of the app reached through More no longer shows two back buttons: the tab bar is Record, Library, Contacts, Vaults and More, and More is now the app's own list of the other parts, grouped as the sidebar groups them, each opening with its own single navigation bar. iPad and Mac record screen, from the screenshots: the recipient chips wrap onto a second line instead of being cut ("Maria (in"), and while recording the time sits above the button.

A fourth Lab experiment, L04, live labels, from the owner's voice note. While you speak, Apple's on-device model is asked every few seconds to fill in a small set of labels from the words so far: who the note is for (matched to a contact or an agent, with their avatar), its topic, title and urgency, and others you switch on. They appear as a grid of chips that update live. What you say a label is, stands: say this is a memo for the website conductor, or no, the topic is something else, and that label is pinned and the model can no longer move it; tapping a label does the same. After every loop a small notice says how long the model took to its first label and in all, about how many tokens were sent, and which labels changed, and every loop goes into a log that can be shared as JSON. You choose how often it asks and how many of the words it sends. The experiment keeps no recording and no note. In test: no loop has been run against a model, so its speed is not yet known.

The voice game shows what it hears, at the owner's request ("the game is so cool"): while Listen is on, a line under the board shows the sentence being said, black once settled and grey while it may still change, and the last four sentences with what each became (the command and which engine, refused, not understood, or asking the model) and its time; the command also sits beside the large time. The board takes the house palette, and Play as me puts your own avatar on the board in Boxes. Play opens on a landing page: the two games as large tiles with a picture of their first level, your best score and where you are, how to start, and how the last game went; a tile opens that game.

The Guide, after the owner found it had little to do on a wide Mac window: it opens on the latest release card, large, with Try buttons that open the sections the card names; on iPad and Mac it has two columns, the list on the left and the chosen card, guide or list on the right; every guide is a picture tile, and a guide shows each picture beside its numbered notes with an Open button for its section; the ideas are a count per status and what is in progress now. After the owner's second note: back and forward in the Guide as in a browser (two buttons, a sideways swipe, Command-[ and Command-]), a few lines before every picture saying what it shows and why it matters, a contents row at the top of each guide to jump to its parts, and wider pages.

notes: The record screen on iPad and Mac is two columns, at the owner's request: on the left who it is for, the control, and while recording the live words and attachments; on the right your recent notes, Messages from Claude (from your agents vault) and Explore. iPhone keeps one column. Play has its own drawing.

A wide record screen for iPad and Mac, ready to be wired: two columns that scroll on their own, what you do on the left (who it is for, the control, the live words) and what came back on the right (recent notes, Claude's replies as a conversation), held to readable widths.

Two ways to talk says where a shared vault is used now: in VoiceDebrief, the Agents vault you share with Claude; in SGit Vaults, a vault shared with the people you choose (it had said shared vaults with people were still to come). The Play section has its own drawing: a board of squares beside a figure carrying a lantern up a ladder.

The secrets app article grows, after more from the owner: how the iCloud file stays whole when two devices or two people write at once (never replace a copy that has not been merged; a merge the app shows you), where that is weaker than the server and when the server is worth paying for; the comparison as positioning, including where 1Password, Bitwarden and Proton Pass already share with public keys; and pricing costed against what each operation costs, with a recommendation: credit only, a £5 starter that switches on a server copy charged per change, reading never charged. Read it.

A research article for a separate secrets app, from the owner's voice note: other password managers compared, the vault kept as one encrypted file in your own iCloud Drive with past copies and a merge after offline edits, several stores, who holds the key (iCloud Keychain, a passkey, a printed code), names and a build plan. Proposed, nothing built. Read it.

Fixes a crash on starting a recording (0.1.91 on the owner's iPhone, read from the TestFlight crash report): the live words' microphone tap is now put on cleanly, in the microphone's own format. And silent recordings: when no sound reaches the recorder for three seconds, the live words are stopped so the recording gets the microphone (every silent note so far was made while the live words ran). A new workflow reads the crash reports testers share.

The Lab's control centre shows more of what it is doing, after the owner tried it ("really cool") and asked to see everything being heard and to follow the flow. While it listens, a strip at the top shows the words as they arrive, the ones that may still change in grey. Below, every sentence heard has its own numbered card, newest first, whether or not it led to an action: what was heard, what the fixed phrases made of it and which phrase it was, what the model made of it and how long it took, what was proposed, and what happened.
External TestFlight: the newest build replaces any still waiting for Apple's Beta App Review (the waiting one is expired), at the owner's direction; a build already in review is left to finish.

Play is a section of its own in the sidebar (after Agents), with the voice games that were in the Lab as L03, at the owner's request ("brilliant; make them a top-level item"). L03 stays in the Lab too.
Command-Return sends: in the picture sheet, the Talk banner and an agent's message box, at the owner's request.

While recording, add a picture and a line to the note: a picture on the clipboard is offered at once ("A picture is on the clipboard: add it to this note"), or paste or choose one; it goes with the note to whoever it is for. The record screen says when a newer build is waiting in TestFlight, from the report Claude writes into your vault, with a button to open TestFlight.

The voice game (Lab, L03: Play) lets go of the microphone as the control centre does: it stops listening when you leave the screen or the app goes to the background, never switches the audio off for the rest of the app, gives up if it was stopped while starting, and will not start while a voice note is being recorded. A results page on the site, L03 results, is written from the logs the app shares: drop one in website/lab/l03/runs/ and run the generator. No run yet.

Two ways to talk, at the owner's request: a lane (one way, sealed to their key, you cannot read it back) and a shared vault (both of you read and write the same encrypted files) each have an animated drawing, a small badge for any message or send, and a short explainer with both side by side. Ready to be placed on the send card, Messages and Agents.

Messages to Claude reads as a conversation: your notes on the right in the accent colour with their state beneath, Claude's replies on the left beside its conductor avatar. The picture sheet opens with who the picture goes to (you, an arrow, them), and its states take the house symbols and colours. A palette and a player sprite (your own avatar) are offered to the L03 game.

The vault list in the vault colour: each vault has an indigo badge (a shield for read and write, an eye for read only), and its status line carries a symbol and colour for where it is: in step with its server (green), not yet pushed or ahead (amber), push failed (red), on the server only (indigo). The words are unchanged.

The workbench in the app: "Open the workbench" on Agents opens your shared vault in the web Vault inside VoiceDebrief: a chat with Claude, how we work, and mock-ups Claude changes without an app build. The conversation with an agent shows newest first, with your own words above each answer. An Overview button closes an agent.

Agents: "Give this vault to Claude" is now a large button that shows "Sending, sealed to Claude's key", then "Given to Claude" with a green confirmation, and cannot be pressed again by mistake (the owner pressed it four times because nothing showed it had gone).

A fix in the Lab's control centre, found while looking for why three notes from 0.1.72 arrived as silence. Its Listen switched the shared audio session off when it stopped, a moment after the screen was left: if a note was being recorded by then, or already was when Listen was pressed, that could switch the microphone off underneath the recording. A Listen still waiting for the microphone permission could also start after the screen had gone. The Lab now never switches the audio session off, does not listen while a note is being recorded, gives up a start that was overtaken by a stop, and stops when the app leaves the foreground. Whether this was the cause of those three notes is not known.

Agents: choosing a vault now sticks (the picker stayed on None and "Give this vault to Claude" did nothing, found by the owner), and it says when there is no vault to choose. Talking to Claude: the banner takes a picture (paste or choose) and a line of text, with a Send button; they go with the note.

Talking to Claude from any screen now shows what is being heard: a banner above the button with the live words, the time, the level and how to send, at the owner's request ("I need a visual clue, show me the text").

The pictures of every screen: the picture of what the app asks before sending to the developer finds its button by a word in its name, after the button was renamed and the run failed with every picture taken. Nothing in the app has changed.

The sgit app draws who you trust: you in the middle, each person around you with their photo, the line solid when you both have each other's card and dashed when only you have theirs. From the map, make a shared vault for chosen people: the vault's key is sealed to each person's key and sent to their inbox, and the vault shows who it is shared with
The sgit app gains People: your card as a QR code, contacts you add by scanning (with a photo of the person, kept on your device), an inbox for sealed messages, and Keys and access under Secrets

The sgit app keeps a small picture and the facts of every file in the vault beside it, so a folder of large videos shows its pictures without anyone downloading the videos: the picture (a photo, a frame of a video, a page of a document) and a facts file (size, dimensions, length, codec, camera, when it was taken; where only if you allow it) in a hidden .sgit folder that any client can read

Faces in more places: each contact in Contacts shows its avatar, an agent's conversation opens with you, an arrow and the agent, and the card that follows a send shows the same route above its steps. A contact is drawn the same way everywhere (Claude, the built-in recipient, as a conductor).

A game played by voice, Lab experiment L03 (issue 300), from the owner's note while driving. Under Settings, Lab, L03: Play. Two small games on the same pieces: Boxes (squares from above: find the gold, the exit opens, keys, doors, traps, three levels) and Lantern (a figure from the side: walk, jump, climb ladders, three levels). Say or type a command: the phrases (code, no model) act at once, and Apple's on-device model is asked when they find nothing, with only the tools that make sense at that moment; its first tool call ends the request, and the code checks and applies it. Every command shows the time from the end of your words to the move, which engine acted, the model's time to its tool call, estimated tokens and energy; the log is shared as JSON. A clue appears when you look stuck: first a glowing square, then the words to try, phrased by the model when it is there. A voice player can play the game by itself: it says its commands aloud (and makes the odd mistake), the microphone hears them like yours, and its times run from the moment its voice stops. A few things are hidden. In test: compiled and unit tested, never played on a device or put to a model.

The Lab's control centre (L02) gains a third action it can carry out: record a note for a named person. It always waits for Do it and cannot be switched to go ahead by itself, because a note recorded for a person is sent to them when it is finished; the card says so before the button is pressed, and afterwards shows what the app answered, including a refusal when no contact has that name. The Lab's side only: until the Record screen is connected to it, the card says recording is not connected. A correction made afterwards in the log no longer carries anything out.

Three notes from 0.1.72 arrived as pure silence (-91 dB throughout): nothing reached the microphone. While recording, the app now says so after three seconds of true silence ("No sound is reaching the microphone: another app may be using it"), so a silent recording is noticed at once. A quiet room does not trigger it.

The record screen shows who a note is from and who it goes to: your face, an arrow, and the chosen contact's (Claude drawn as the conductor), at the owner's request. Choose your own photo or another generated look under Identity.

Avatars, at the owner's request: every person and agent has a face, a photo if one is set (kept on the device) or a character generated from their key or id, the same on every device. Kinds have frames: green for you, gold with a baton for a conductor, indigo for a session, dashed for a sub-agent. A route picture (you, an arrow, who the note goes to, or several) and a "How you look" section are ready to be placed on the record and Identity screens.

Design, second batch: a note's row carries at most one mark, as a pill in words and its colour: what is working now, a send or a save that did not happen (red), a note that was interrupted or had no words (amber), or the vault it was saved to (indigo). The note screen's state lines take the same symbols and colours. The Lab's experiments have icons; colours in the note parts, the Lab and Contacts are the house palette.

The sgit app plays videos: a play mark on each video, a Play button that decrypts and plays it with sound (even on silent), full screen, and a picture from the video on its tile once it has been played

The sgit app has a Guide on its home list: what is new in each version, a guide with numbered pictures for each part (getting started, inside a vault, sharing, secrets), and every idea with where it stands

The Lab's control centre (L02) now carries out two confirmed actions, the two that are safe to undo: opening a section of the app, and finding a note, which only reads the library and lists what it found on the card. Nothing happens before Do it, unless that action is switched to go ahead without asking. The other five actions are still recorded only, and each card says which it was. In test: no sentence has been put to a model.

The sgit app gains People (not yet on its root list): your card as a QR code and a link, contacts added by scanning, a picture or a link, with a photo of the person offered after scanning in person, an inbox that checks for new messages, and Keys and access for the keys your identity holds. Keys are made only when you ask.

The articles can be read inside the app, under Guide, Articles (and SGit Vaults has its own copy to show, with its design pages); a design page can list its ideas for the ideas tracker under a heading Ideas. Release cards: an ASCII box per change, written to website/versions/next/, moved onto the version's page at release with the version and date filled in, and shown at the top of What is new; this release carries the first. A fourth guide for SGit Vaults: secrets, one secret, and the questions for the owner.

+----------------------------------------------------------------------+

notes: Claude's replies in the app: a bubbles button on the record screen opens Messages to Claude, with Claude's answer under each note it answers and a From Claude section. They come from the vault you give Claude on the Agents screen, written there encrypted, so only your devices read them.

A note made for someone (a contact or Claude) goes as soon as its transcript is ready, without a debrief: the owner found the wait broke his flow, and the recipient reads the transcript (on his 13:31 note the debrief took 10.4 s after a 7 s transcript). A note for "Just me" is debriefed as before.

Send a picture, at the owner's request: on the record screen, "Paste screenshot" takes a picture from the clipboard and "Choose picture" one from Photos; add a line, pick who it is for, and Send. It goes encrypted over the same lane as a voice note, with the same five tries.

From the owner's drive, where signal came and went: a send that fails is tried five times (10 s, 30 s, 1 min, 2 min apart) and at once when iOS says the network is back, with "No connection, trying again in ..." and Try now on the card; after five tries, Send again, and it goes once more when the signal returns or the app opens. A sent note now ends in a large green "Sent to ... at ..." with a success tap, held for ten seconds.

The level bars while recording, after the owner's second note on them ("very noisy", and not red): room noise shows as nothing, the bars rise quickly and fall slowly so they follow the voice rather than every sample, they are shorter, and they are drawn in the app's own colour.

"Send this now" from the owner's test of 0.1.55: it took two tries. The pause before it acts is no longer restarted each time the recogniser repeats or settles the same words; only words that undo it cancel it.

The sgit app becomes a secrets manager, first part. Secrets on the home list: passwords, device passcodes, Wi-Fi, cards, tokens and keys, each kept as one encrypted file in a vault, hidden values behind Face ID, a strong-password maker. Questions for you: the people building the app ask, and you answer by choosing, typing or speaking. The design, with drawings, is on the site. Your iPhone, iPad and Mac now open the same vaults with nothing to set up: vault keys and the access key are kept in iCloud Keychain (a switch in Settings), and vaults from your other devices appear when the app comes to the front. Sharing with people comes next

The sgit app: an experiment with Apple Intelligence. On a vault's three dots, Ask this vault puts one question to Apple's on-device model, which may look at the names, sizes, folders and history through four small tools, each call shown under the answer. It sees no file's contents, changes nothing, and nothing leaves the device. Untried on a device

A second Lab experiment, L02, the control centre, from the owner's notes while driving: giving instructions is a different mode from thinking aloud. Under Settings, Lab: say, type or replay a sentence, and two engines each say which action it asks for, the fixed phrases (now a list you can see and change, kept on the device) and Apple's on-device model, asked one sentence at a time with one tool for each action. Each proposed action is a card that waits: Do it, Not this, or Edit. An action can be marked to go ahead without asking. Fourteen test sentences, some said in words no phrase holds and some that are not instructions at all, count how often each engine is right and how long the model takes; the log is exported as JSON. The experiment carries no action out: nothing is recorded, sent, saved or opened. In test: it compiles and its logic is unit tested, but no sentence has been put to a model.

A visual identity for both apps, at the owner's request: the identity sets one family (a navy ground, green for VoiceDebrief, indigo for SGit Vaults and for vaults in both), one symbol, colour and picture per section, a type scale, spacing and corners, all in a small design system in each app. New app icons for both. The record screen's Explore tiles each have a drawing, a banner greets the first visit, and the record control has the house green and a ring; SGit Vaults turns indigo, with a banner when there are no vaults. Two infographics on the site: the life of a voice note, and the family.

SGitPeople's messages are now pki.sgit.ai's own (its message form, signed inside and out, handed over as its m1 code), so pki.sgit.ai's pages and agent tool read what the apps send; checked against pki.sgit.ai's code in a new workflow. A reply names the note it answers, for the talk-to-the-developer button. An invitation expires after seven days, and a newcomer may show pki.sgit.ai's k1 key code instead of a card.

Three guides for SGit Vaults, in VoiceDebrief's Guide and on the site's guides: getting started (open a vault you were sent, or make one), inside a vault and its history, and sharing, each a picture of the screen with numbered arrows.

The sgit app keeps a record of what you do in it (Settings, Your activity): every screen and how long it was open, and every action, with no file names, vault names or keys. A button sends it, encrypted, to the developer. Each device keeps its own. The whole web Vault opens inside the app on the vault or the file you are looking at (three dots, Open in the web Vault): folders, HTML preview, Markdown, editing. It opens looking only; Allow changes lets it save. Also new on the site: a guide to the app in pictures, with the things to press numbered

Agents, a new section made for iPad: how many agents are working for you, waiting or idle; each with its role, what it is doing and what it waits for; and a conversation with each. It is drawn from a report the conductor (Claude) writes into a vault of yours: you choose the vault and give it to Claude, its key sealed on the device to Claude's key. Messages to an agent go over its lane, or through Claude when it has none; replies come back in the report. The app refreshes every two minutes while you are there.

From the owner's notes while driving: "send this now" no longer fires on "don't send it now", and waits for a pause, so saying it in passing does not stop the recording; the words that act are shown under the control while recording. The level bars stay pinned with the control and are less sensitive, so speech no longer looks maxed out. The On this device and Network panel becomes two small icons in the bar, steady, green while in use; tap them for what each means and a log of what happened.

A Guide, for finding out what exists: every idea and request for both apps, from the issues, the articles and the reality files, with its status (seen working, built untried, in progress, proposed, parked), where it is in the app, the versions that named it and the sentence that decided its status, searchable in the app and on the site's new ideas page; What is new, every version newest first with those since you last looked marked; and a guide per feature (record, a note, the library, vaults, sending, the briefing, settings), each a picture of the screen with numbered arrows, in the app and as the site's new guides. A welcome for the first launch is written, and three journeys (the owner, a new tester, a teammate sent a vault). The Guide and the welcome appear once they are given their place in the app's shell. Generated by website/admin/ideas.mjs, never written by hand.

A new shared package, SGitPeople, the layer under both apps for people, messages and secrets (issue 200). The key bundle (PKIKit) and the lane envelope move into it from VoiceDebrief, unchanged. New in it, not yet on any screen: a signed contact card that fits a QR code, contacts with how each was met, sealed and signed messages, an inbox client tested against answers recorded from the live server, when to check for new messages, a secrets store that remembers who holds each secret, and the first exchange that gives a newcomer the access key.

After the owner's test on a Mac: the record control is at the top of the record screen and larger (pinned above the live words while recording); the contact chips are centred under the title instead of escaping to the edge; and the card after a note finished for someone shows its journey step by step (recorded, written up, encrypted and sent, part by part) with what goes, clearing itself once sent. No OK to press; Do not send only until sending starts.

External testers get builds regularly: a new workflow puts a dev build of either app in front of its public TestFlight link when the commit says [external], when the version ends in 0, or by hand; it waits for processing, writes What to Test from that version's page, adds the build to the external group and submits it for Beta App Review.

For driving, at the owner's request: say "send this now" (or "stop recording") at the end of a recording to finish it without a tap; the play/pause button on headphones, a car or the lock screen also finishes it (untried: iOS may not send those to a recording app). Talk to Claude: a button on every screen but Record; tap, speak, tap, and it goes to Claude (developer); hold it for Messages to Claude, every note you sent and where it stands. Replies arrive there once the app has its own inbox.

The sgit app at the largest text sizes: a folder is shown as a list, so that file names are not cut short, and the iPad's folder tree is wider. Found by new pictures in dark appearance and at a large text size (22 screens)

Every part of the app is in plain sight, at the owner's request: the sidebar (tabs and More on iPhone) now lists Record, Library, Contacts, Vaults, and under You: Identity, Credit, Your activity; under Experiments: Lab, Your words; under More: What this build does, Settings. The record screen ends with Explore: a tile for every section. Your activity: every screen opened and for how long, and the main actions, kept on the device with no content, and a button to send it to Claude (developer).

The record screen is contact-driven, at the owner's request: above the record control, choose who the note is for (Just me, Claude (developer), or anyone you have added; the choice is remembered). Recording for someone means finishing is the send: tap to record, tap to finish, and it goes when it is written up, with Do not send on the card that follows. The built-in recipient is now called Claude (developer). The Lab is under Settings, Experiments.

The sgit app: when adding to a shared vault is refused for want of an access key, the message says the access key is separate from the vault key and who to ask; the file is kept and can be tried again. A picture of that state joins the others (18 screens). How a teammate should get the right to add is still the owner's decision (issue 110)

The sgit app after its first review (issues 111 to 116): a line on every folder says whether everything is on the server, on this device only or on its way in; Share is on the toolbar and opens with a message to send that carries the steps for the receiver; the Create sheet's server switch is off for a person with no access key; a whole folder can be saved out to Files as the originals; the share sheet gives the line to paste on a computer to clone the vault; History is grouped by day and says whether a commit was made by this device or another; four more pictures of screens the review could not see. Not yet used on a device

Review round 3: five synthetic users on the pictures of finish and send, the briefing on opening and where the work happens. Three of round 2's findings are seen to be fixed; fifteen new ones, the first that a send cannot be stopped where it is pressed and is lost if the app is closed before it goes (issues 043 to 045). Nothing in the app has changed.

After review round 3: a send that is waiting is kept on the note, so closing the app does not forget it, and goes when the app next opens; a failed send is kept and said on the row, the note and the briefing; the card after Finish and send has Do not send; a note already sent to someone asks before sending again (issue 043). The balance and the version show as words in the bar, and Discard moves to the right while recording (044). Settings and the status screen say what is true: an interrupted recording is always kept, and vault keys are in iCloud Keychain by default (045). Rows say when a note was sent; the briefing keeps to three lines.

The sgit app gains a gallery: a list of vaults to show somebody, by topic, each opened in the web Vault in a browser inside the app. The list is data, added on the device or read from a showcase.json in a vault; it ships empty. Also a picture of every screen of the sgit app from CI, and fixes those pictures called for.

A briefing when you open the app (issue 025): after an update, "Updated to this version: see what is new", linking to its page; and what happened since you last looked: new notes and their length, interrupted ones to run again, who notes were sent to, what was saved to your vault and what could not be. Worked out by the app from the library, not written by a model.

The sgit app: a vault is created on the device with no access token and no network, and takes files at once; sharing it sends it to the server, which is the first time a token is asked for. Forgetting a vault that is only on the device warns that it deletes it. In the engine, VaultSync can move a vault that holds large files. At the owner's request after the first run: the access key can be typed on the Create screen and the new vault goes to the server at once; files and folders can be dropped in from the desktop and dragged out; on an iPad or a Mac the folders are a tree down the left.

Vault keys and server tokens in iCloud Keychain, on by default (issue 017, the owner's decision). Each vault's key, each server and each token is now a Keychain item of its own, kept on this device and, unless a new switch under Keys on the Vaults tab is turned off, in iCloud Keychain too, so that a vault made on one device can appear on the owner's others and survive losing a device. A vault whose key has arrived says where the vault itself is: on its server, or still only on another device. Turning the switch off moves everything back to this device only. The key that signs a device's commits is never synchronised. In test: the logic is unit-tested with an in-memory Keychain; that Apple carries the items between two real devices has not been seen.

Where the work happens, on the record screen: one line for this device (listening, Apple's speech model transcribing, Apple's model writing the debrief) and one for the network (sending to whom, which part, encrypted), green while each is busy (issue 027).

Finish and send in one press: while recording, a button for each of your own recipients finishes the note, sends it as soon as it is written up, and leaves you on the record screen for the next one (issue 026). Sends now go one after another, so several notes sent in quick succession all go. A note remembers who it was sent to and when, on the note and in the list.
A version badge at the top of the record and library screens, beside the balance, opens this version's own page of what changed. CI now writes that page for every release from the notes headed next.

After review round 2: a recording can be shared or saved to Files from its note (039); deleting a note, throwing away a recording and sending to the developer ask with an alert that always shows how to say no (040); Diagnostics no longer offers a lane link that nothing used (041); the balance reads "Test credit" and says recording never stops (032); the send bar is shorter; a time reads 00:03, not 0:03; a note never transcribed offers "Transcribe and debrief".

Review round 1, the rest of this session's findings: a recording can start while the last note is still being written up; notes wait their turn and say so (issue 030). States say what to do: an interrupted note says to open it and run it again, a note with no debrief says why, an untranscribed note is no longer titled Recording, and the record screen promises it saves as you speak before you start (issue 036).

After the first review by synthetic users (round 1): a note opens with its one sentence as the heading and the date beneath; the clean text experiment moves below the transcript; every note with audio has a player, and tapping a transcript line plays from there; the send bar appears only when there is something to send, lists your own recipients first, names the built-in one as the developer of this test build, and says what goes; lists hold a readable width on iPad; Recent says the day; a cut title ends with an ellipsis; the toolbar says the language rather than its code; one line, not 1 lines.

Pictures of every screen (issue 016). A debug build launched with -VDSampleData is given invented notes in a temporary folder, a vault book in memory with one invented vault in the same folder, and no network, never the real library or Keychain, and -VDScreen opens a named screen; none of it is compiled into a release build. A UI test target takes one screenshot per screen, and a new workflow, screens.yml, runs it on an iPhone and an iPad simulator in light and dark and keeps the PNGs, with a contact sheet per set, as an artifact named by commit. Build, test and release says how to fetch them from a Linux container. Nothing a user sees has changed.

Identity (issues 005 and 018). PKIKit: the sgit key bundle in Swift (RSA-OAEP 4096 and ECDSA P-256, fingerprints, PKCS#8, keys under a passphrase, the k1 key code, detached signatures, statements, the signed envelope), proven in a new workflow where sgit pki and pki.sgit.ai's own keys.js read what Swift makes and Swift reads what they make. In the app, under Settings, an Identity screen: a key pair that says who you are, kept in iCloud Keychain so it reaches your other devices; a second key that says which device, kept in the Secure Enclave where there is one and ended by deleting the app; a statement, signed by the first and kept in a vault, that vouches for the second; and, optionally, a delegation from an identity at pki.sgit.ai, with the answer pasted back in. In test: none of it has run on a device, and debriefs are not yet signed by the device key.

Credit, on the pattern of newsroom.sgit.ai's meter (issue 008). A balance that starts at £5.00, is charged a little for just about everything the user does (a transcript by the minute, a debrief, a clean passage, creating a vault, each file saved to one, sending, and so on, in whole pence), and may go below zero with nothing blocked; recording is never charged. A counter on the Record and Library screens opens the credit screen: the balance, top-up, takings by feature, every entry, the prices. A charge can be declined with a reason. No money changes hands: the top-up is simulated and says so; paying through the App Store is written and switched off until the products exist. Every price is a placeholder. The ledger is a file on the device that nothing checks. Credit explains it, with what Apple requires. In test: not yet seen on a device.

A second app begins in this repository, for now: the sgit app (Apps/SGit, bundle ai.sgit.vaults.app), sgit as a native app, starting with photos, videos and large files into a vault. Its design and its own reality file are under sgit-app. The vault engine reads and writes files over 4 MB as sgit does (issue 023), encrypting from disk to disk, checked against sgit in both directions by a new workflow, sgit-app.yml. Nothing of the sgit app has run on a device. The version is now CI's, as in the other VoiceDebrief repositories: every push to dev is tagged with the next number, the version file and the README badge are written by CI, and the site is stamped when it is deployed. The app's TestFlight version is that tag.

The Lab, and its first experiment. Under Settings, a Lab section with L01, one prompt with tools on and off: type or pick a prompt, switch each tool on or off, and send one request to Apple's on-device model in a new session. The screen then shows everything: the instructions and prompt sent, the tools offered and kept back, each tool call with its arguments, result and time, the answer, the total time, and any error in plain words. Four tools that only read: the date and time, a list of notes, one note's transcript, and a choice of next screen that is recorded and not acted on. Six preset prompts say which tools a reliable model would call, and the screen counts how often it did. Runs are kept while the app is open and exported as JSON. Every request goes through one component, the model door, with a policy and a record; the debrief does not use it yet. In test: it compiles and its logic is unit tested, but CI has no model, so no request has been made.

After the owner's notes on build 0.1.9: the Send buttons are a bar fixed at the bottom of a note, where the growing transcript and debrief cannot move them, and a note sent before it is finished goes the moment it is. The version is shown on the record screen and links here.

Finishing a note saves it to a vault, at the owner's request (issue 022): once the note is done and its audio compressed, it is written into the vault chosen in Settings as one signed commit. On by default, with a switch; nothing happens until a vault exists. The note says where it was saved, or why it was not.

Vaults are local first, and a server is a remote. Creating a vault no longer asks for an access token: a vault is made, saved into, read and browsed on the device, with no server and no network. Servers are added by name, with an address and an access token in the Keychain; a vault has none or one. Push and pull are separate, explicit steps that only ever move a branch forward: when the device and the server have both changed, the app says a merge is needed (not built) and overwrites nothing. Each vault says where it is: on this device only, not yet pushed, on the server too, ahead of it, or push failed and why. Vaults made by earlier builds (from v0.1.5) stay on their server and work as before, and can be copied to the device. Forgetting a vault now asks first and says what would be lost. In test: none of this has run on a device, and nothing has been pushed to a real server from the app. CI has sgit clone a vault that was created in one folder and pushed to another.

The version is now CI's, as in the other VoiceDebrief repositories: every push to dev is tagged with the next number, the version file and the README badge are written by CI, and the site is stamped when it is deployed. The app's TestFlight version is that tag.

Recipients. A note can be sent to anybody who has given you their lane: a person, another device, an agent session. Add one under Settings or from a note by scanning their QR code with the camera, choosing a picture of it, or pasting the link; the code may carry their name. A note has one Send button per recipient. A recipient's own QR code can be shown, to pass them on. The developer's lane built into the test build is the first recipient and still asks before sending; one you added yourself sends at once. For the other side, tools/conductor/conductor.py makes an inbox (a key pair, a vault, a lane), prints its link or QR code, and opens what arrives. The app now asks for the camera, only to read a QR code. In test: nothing here has run on a device. A later build of this version changes the record control, at the owner's request: it is green, and while recording shows a tick and finishes the note; Discard is a small red word at the top that asks before deleting.

An experiment, at the owner's suggestion: a clean text. A note can be rewritten as full sentences by Apple's model, a passage of about 110 words at a time, with nothing meant to be left out. The model is given the speaker's own words (Settings, Your words), because Apple's speech model cannot be: SpeechTranscriber ignores contextual strings. It returns structure, not prose (guided generation), including up to three phrases per passage it could not follow, each with a question; an answer is kept and joins the speaker's words. The screen can show what was changed, word by word, and warns when a rewrite is under half the length of what was said. The clean text travels with a note sent over the lane. Also: the record screen follows the live words. In test: no clean text has been made on a device.

Build A of the design: capture without loss, and a new shell. A note is created when recording starts and the recording is written straight into it as WAV, a form that can be repaired if the app dies before the file is closed; it is compressed only after the note is finished. A call or another app taking the microphone ends the recording and keeps it. Every note is kept on the device: a Library tab lists them by day and a note can be reopened, run again or deleted. Stopping opens the note at once and it fills in. Four tabs (Record, Library, Vaults, Settings) that become a sidebar on wide screens; a record screen with one large control; developer tools moved under Settings. The background audio mode is declared; recording with the screen locked is untested. A later build of the same version makes the record screen follow the live words, after the owner found they ran off the bottom.

The debrief prompt again, after the first note sent over the developer lane: the model wrote "Speaker is..." and "[Speaker]" because the prompt itself said "the speaker". It now says the note is the reader's own, asks for plain statements with no subject, and marks the reader's tasks [me].

Vaults. The vault engine can now create a vault, in the form sgit init writes; CI has sgit clone a vault Swift created. A Vaults tab: keep an SG/Send access token in the Keychain, create a vault, add one made elsewhere by its key, and look inside (head, files, history, branches, the key, and every request, decryption and signature check the engine made). After a run, save the debrief, transcript, run and audio into a vault as one signed commit. In test: no vault has been created from a device yet.

The developer's lane is built into the test build, at the owner's request, so a note can be sent without pasting a link first; a pasted link still takes its place. Sending still happens only when the button is pressed.

While recording: the words appear as they are spoken, and moving bars show the microphone is being heard. The live text is a preview; the transcript that is kept is still made from the recorded file when the recording stops. And a way to help judge the models: with a lane link pasted on the Diagnostics tab, a button after each run sends that note (audio, transcript and debrief) to the developer over an sgit append lane, encrypted on the device to the developer's key. Nothing is sent without pressing it.

The debrief prompt, changed after the first real runs on an iPhone and a Mac: the model was copying quotation marks from the prompt's examples, renaming a heading, repeating a one-line note back as its own key point, and turning a passing remark into an action. The prompt now shows the shape with no quotation marks, says the speaker's own tasks are theirs, and says what is not an action. A note of fewer than 25 words is no longer sent to the model: the transcript is the whole note.

The first feature, as the plan's quality spike: record a voice note or choose an audio file, transcribe it on the device with Apple's SpeechAnalyzer, and write a debrief with Apple's on-device model, reading a long note in parts. A diagnostics screen reports what the device says about both models and exports it. Nothing is saved yet. In test: nobody has judged the results on a device. Also: the TestFlight upload, proven by build 0.1.0 (4), installed on an iPhone and a Mac.

The repository starts. An iPhone and iPad app that builds and tests, with one screen that says what is and is not built. The SGitVault vault engine copied from PrompTugal__App__iOS, with the door derivation made to work for any site and checked against the published vector. CI: build and test on a Mac, vault interop with sgit, and this site. The plan, published.
